cases.title: 1 divided by 3 times 3 displays as 1 via guard-digit rounding
cases.notes: The only worked example on pages 84-87. Guidebook prints the display as a bare '1' and does not state DEC; at the default DEC=2 a real unit would show '1.00'. The load-bearing claim is that the INTERNAL result is 0.9999999999999 and only the display rounds up. Does not discriminate AOS from CHN: x and / share priority 4 (p. 87), so both evaluate left-to-right and both yield 1.

cases.title: Internal value of 1 divided by 3 is 13 significant digits
cases.notes: Step 1 of the p. 86 example, printed literally in the guidebook. This is the INTERNAL 13-digit value, NOT the display -- at 10 displayed digits the screen would read 0.3333333333. Asserts the guard-digit mantissa width. Implementations using IEEE doubles will hold ~0.333333333333333 and must truncate to 13 significant digits to match.

cases.title: Internal value of 0.3333333333333 times 3 is 0.9999999999999
cases.notes: Step 2 of the p. 86 example, printed literally. Critical parity assertion: the internal result is NOT exactly 1. Chained arithmetic must consume the 13-digit internal value, never the rounded display. An implementation that computes exactly 1.0 internally passes the visible example by luck and diverges elsewhere.
